- Expected steady-state: ~120 reqs/sec (p50), peak bursts up to ~450 reqs/sec during morning and early-evening spikes.

Thanks Samira — great context and thanks for the CSV. Quick read, looks representative. High-level answers and proposed next steps below.

Ballpark unit economics (enterprise PoC / initial estimate):
- Baseline target: $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens (depends on model family + quantization).
- Streaming premium: expect ~15–25% uplift if you require token-streaming paths with lower batching windows.

Batching & concurrency assumptions for continuous-batching workloads:
- Continuous batching window: 40–70 ms recommended for chat-style UIs where p50 latency target is ~150–300 ms.
- Effective batch size: with your steady-state (120 req/s) and 40–70 ms window, expect continuous batch sizes of 5–9 for short-context chats; bursts drive higher batch sizes.
- Concurrency handling: autoscale concurrent worker slots to absorb 2–3x peak QPS for short bursts (i.e., configure burst capacity).
- Streaming: route streaming requests to a smaller-batch low-latency pool (higher cost), and non-streaming to larger-batch pools.

Suggested PoC (2 weeks):
1) Lab: Redwood hosted PoC with a dedicated execution pool sized for your peak (we'll propose exact vGPU counts after we verify avg tokens/sec).
2) Goals: validate p95 latency under bursts, measure tokens/sec per GPU, and compute a 1M-token cost estimate with your mix (streaming vs non-streaming).
3) Deliverables: PoC performance report, cost projection ($/1M tokens), and a recommended production config.

What we need from you:
- Full 48-hour sample of production traffic (CSV or S3 link) ideally with timestamps and streaming_flag.
- Primary SLA/latency targets (p50/p95) and any regulatory constraints (data residency).
- Procurement contact to issue an initial estimate/POC SOW.

I've looped Vanessa (pricing) and Monica (solutions/ops) — they'll help scope the PoC and build the estimate. We'll follow up with a short tech deep-dive tomorrow if that works.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Subject: Internal: quick PoC sizing assumptions for Lighthouse Health

Internal note — quick numerical assumptions based on Samira's sample and the CSV they attached: 

- Observed averages (sample): tokens_in ~600, tokens_out ~120, streaming_flag ~35%.
- Tokens per request (total): ~720 tokens. At 120 rps steady -> ~86.4k tokens/sec (steady). Peak 450 rps -> ~324k tokens/sec.
- GPU throughput (reference, mixed GGML optimized model): ~45k tokens/sec per vGPU under continuous batching (batch window 50ms, effective batch size ~7).
- Estimated GPUs required: steady: 2 vGPU; peak: 8 vGPU (accounting for overhead + headroom).

Cost math (very rough baseline for PoC):
- If we price at $950 / 1M tokens (mid of Aditya's band), steady-state cost per second: 86.4k tokens/sec -> ~0.0864M tokens/sec -> $82 / sec? (note: convert units carefully)
- Better to express monthly: 1M tokens priced at $950 means 1M tokens costs $950. If they consume X tokens/month we scale. We'll produce a clearer token-month projection in the estimate.

Operational recommendations:
- Continuous-batching window: 40–60ms for mixed workloads; keep a separate low-latency pool for streaming requests with target batching window <= 20–30ms.
- Cache: prefix KV caching for frequent prompts to reduce token load (saves up to 12–18% tokens for repetitive prompts).

I'll draft a small estimate spreadsheet with per-GPU token throughput and cost calculation for the PoC.

— Priyom
Principal, Inference Optimization
Redwood Inference
